newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Suspended Africa trade group chief denies charges.
newsitem.headline: Suspended Africa trade group chief denies charges.

text.p: Suspended Common Market of Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chief Bingu Wa Mutharika said on Wednesday he would not cooperate with investigators probing allegations of financial abuses against him.

Mutharika, a Malawian, told a news conference his suspension last week by the COMESA council of ministers was the result of a smear campaign by Malawi's ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) which suspected him of having presidential aspirations.

"The council of ministers was manipulated by the chairman, who is the minister of trade of Malawi, to send me on forced leave without following the due process. The council acted in a manner consistent with a kangaroo court," Mutharika said.
"I do not recognise the manner in which I was sent on forced leave and I will not accept the verdict of the investigation team set up by the council of ministers," he added.
Malawi's trade minister Chakakala Chaziya announced Mutharika's suspension in Lusaka last week claiming he had allegedly misused COMESA funds and abused his authority at the COMESA secretariat.

His suspension shortly followed the pullout of COMESA member states, Mozambique and Lesotho, from the 20-member trade body saying they preferred to work alongside the smaller Southern African Development Community (SADC).
COMESA states include Angola, Burundi, Comoros, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Madagascar, Mauritius, Namibia, Rwanda, Sudan, Swaziland, Tanzania, Uganda, Zaire, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
SADC comprises Mauritius, Angola, Lesotho, Swaziland, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Tanzania, Malawi, South Africa and Botswana.
Mutharika said the council of ministers had no authority to suspend him or to set up a team to investigate him.

"However, I will be glad to appear before a committee duly established by the heads of state (of COMESA) and governments who appointed me and not the council of ministers and I will answer all the charges levelled against me. I am very confident that an impartial and unbiased committee will find me innocent," he said.
